summary:
SMART = Specific, Measurable, Assignable, Realist, Time-related
We created an interactive, collaborative, and innovative game together! ! On the Way to Mars.
Your goal is to manage and succeed in launching a space mission trip

The game helps bridge the gap between spatial concepts and technical decisions

* The content is drawn from resources provided by NASA and the CSA
* Concepts of resource management, decision-making, and exploration under time constraints
* Enabling players to learn through short games and by failing
* A detailed report at the end of the game
* Multiplayer mode available
details: Our project is a training and simulation tool for decision-making under constraints related to time and resource availability. This video game incorporates a Game-Oriented learning aspect. Among the benefits are improved decision-making, a better understanding of space launch missions and engineering concepts based on official NASA documents, and, finally, improved communication when using multiplayer mode. The expected impact is that this project will, we hope, add value to the training of young managers fresh out of school and make data on space launch missions available to anyone who wants to learn about the subject in a fun way. We used C++, Unreal Engine 5.8, an LLM to assist with code writing, Python, and assets from the Fab and CSA public libraries. Our project is creative in its game design, its educational gameplay, and the way it conveys knowledge while linking each decision to the next. Our team has ensured the accuracy of the data used, which is based on NASA resources. Every element or piece of information within the game is accurate and useful in the context of the game, particularly through a post-game analysis that enables players to continuously improve their decision-making.
